Given that 29 of 30 days in each month had no valid data after masking, this comparison rests on essentially one satellite observation per period and should not be treated as a reliable measure of a real month-over-month trend in NO2 over New Jersey — it only shows what the few available pixels say, not a validated seasonal or year-over-year signal. A satellite NO2 column (mol/m^2 or molecules/cm^2) is also a different physical quantity from a ground-level NO2 concentration (ppb), so this does not speak to surface air quality directly.

prompt: Compare the ground NO2 monitors with TROPOMI satellite NO2 over Newark NJ for January 2024.
answer_text:
Exploratory
I was unable to complete a true ground-vs-satellite comparison for Newark, NJ in January 2024. On the monitor side, the only EPA AQS NO2 monitor found near Newark (site 34-017-0006) lies about 83 km outside the Newark area boundary, and EPA AQS returned no daily NO2 readings at all for that monitor over 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-31 (insufficient_evidence, not retriable with the same inputs). So no ground-based NO2 concentration series could be produced for Newark for this period. On the satellite side, I retrieved TEMPO_NO2 (TEMPO_NO2_L3, chosen as the registry's preferred product for tropospheric NO2 column over this area/dates) tropospheric NO2 column data for Newark, which had full valid coverage (31/31 days, valid_fraction 1.0). The area-weighted daily mean series shows values ranging 1.0-4.0 mol/m^2, with an overall period mean of about 2.5 mol/m^2 (sample std ~0.91, n=31 days). Note the satellite product returned is TEMPO, not TROPOMI as requested - the registry selected TEMPO_NO2_L3 as its preferred product for this quantity/area/date combination; no TROPOMI data was retrieved. Also note that a satellite tropospheric NO2 column (mol/m^2) and a ground monitor's surface NO2 concentration (ppb) are physically different quantities - even if ground data had been available, this would not be a direct, like-for-like comparison but two distinct measurements of the same event/location.

prompt: Show me what ozone looked like across the OTC on 2024-07-15.

checks.reason: the ground source was used (monitors/byBox queried)

answer_text:
Exploratory
For 2024-07-15 over the Ozone Transport Region (OTC's 11 states + DC, excluding Northern Virginia), I retrieved TEMPO's total-column ozone product (TEMPO_O3TOT), the registry's preferred satellite dataset for this quantity/area/date — no quality flag variable exists for this product, so all 205 region cells were used unmasked (valid_fraction = 1.0). The map (chart-1) shows total column ozone ranging roughly 286–303 DU across the region on that day, with an area-weighted mean of ~293.7 DU (std ~4.7 DU across cells), a max of 304.0 DU and a min of 285.5 DU. This is a column-density measurement (Dobson Units), not a surface ozone concentration — it reflects ozone through the full atmospheric column (including stratospheric ozone), not ground-level air quality. I attempted to pull EPA AQS ground-monitor ozone data for the same area/date to give a surface-concentration perspective, but AQS returned no active ozone monitors for the area or within 5 degrees of it for 2024-07-15, so no surface AQI-style map is available alongside this (status: insufficient_evidence, not retryable with the same inputs). Note: TEMPO is hourly-capable, but this request used it for a single day as a spatial snapshot; the map shown is a single-day field, not a time-mean composite spanning multiple days.
